items.hook: Dame Beryl Margaret Bainbridge was an English writer.
items.body: She was primarily known for her works of psychological fiction, often macabre tales set among the English working class. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Tropic of Cancer is an autobiographical novel by Henry Miller that is best known as "notorious for its candid sexuality", with the resulting social controversy considered responsible for the "free speech that we now take for granted in literature".
items.body: It was first published in 1934 by the Obelisk Press in Paris, France; however, this edition was banned in the United States. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: In New York City, David Berkowitz (a.k.a. the "Son of Sam") kills one person and seriously wounds another in the first of a series of attacks.
items.body: David Richard Berkowitz, also known as the Son of Sam, the .44 Caliber Killer and the Phantom of the Bronx, is an American serial killer, serial arsonist, and former United States Army soldier who committed a stabbing and a series of shootings in New York City between 1975 and 1977, killing six people and wounding eleven others. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Byzantine–Bulgarian wars: Battle of Kleidion: Byzantine emperor Basil II inflicts a decisive defeat on the Bulgarian army, and his subsequent treatment of 15,000 prisoners reportedly causes Tsar Samuil of Bulgaria to die of a heart attack less than three months later, on October 6.
items.body: The Byzantine–Bulgarian wars were a series of conflicts fought between the Byzantine Empire and the Bulgarian Empire which began after the Bulgars conquered parts of the Balkan peninsula after 680 AD. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Emperor's Candlesticks is a 1937 American historical drama film starring William Powell and Luise Rainer and directed by George Fitzmaurice.
items.body: It is based on the 1899 novel of the same name by Baroness Orczy. One of those things you can't un-know.
